topic: Flow operators: flatMapLatest, combine, zip & debounce

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: `transform` can call `emit` any number of times per upstream value, including zero. For `2` the `if` is false so nothing is emitted; for `1` and `3` it emits twice. `map` would force exactly one value per element.

questions.question: A search screen fires a network request for every query the user types. Which operator makes a new query cancel the request still running for the previous one?
questions.explanation: `flatMapLatest` cancels the inner flow of the previous value as soon as a new upstream value arrives. `flatMapConcat` waits for each request to finish in order, and `flatMapMerge` runs them all concurrently, so stale results could still arrive.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: `zip` pairs values by index and completes as soon as either flow completes, so the extra `3` is never paired. Re-using the latest value of the other flow is what `combine` does, not `zip`.

questions.question: `merge(a, b)` emits every value of `a` first and only then starts emitting the values of `b`.
questions.explanation: `merge` collects all the flows concurrently and emits values as they arrive, so they can interleave. Running one flow to completion before the next is what `flattenConcat` (or `flatMapConcat`) does.

questions.question: A Room query re-emits the whole `User` every time any column changes, but the header only shows `user.name`. Which operator skips emissions where the name didn't change?
questions.explanation: `distinctUntilChangedBy` compares a key from consecutive values and drops a value whose key equals the previous one. `Flow` has no `distinct()` operator, and `debounce` drops values by timing, not by equality.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.code:
import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*

fun main() = runBlocking {
    val result = flowOf(1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 3)
        .distinctUntilChanged()
        .toList()
    println(result)
}
questions.explanation: `distinctUntilChanged` only drops a value that equals the one directly before it. The second `1` group comes after a `2`, so it is emitted again. Removing every duplicate across the whole flow would give `[1, 2, 3]`, which is not what it does.

questions.question: A repository flow can complete without emitting anything when the cache is empty. Which operator lets you emit a placeholder value in exactly that case?
questions.explanation: `onEmpty` runs its block only if the upstream completes normally without emitting any value, and the block may `emit`. `onStart` would emit the placeholder every time, `catch` reacts only to exceptions, and `timeout` throws if no value arrives in time.

questions.question: Which operators can emit MORE than one downstream value for a single upstream value? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: `transform` can call `emit` many times, and `flatMapConcat` emits every value of the inner flow. `map` emits exactly one value per element, while `filter` and `mapNotNull` emit zero or one.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: Once `take(2)` receives its second value it cancels the upstream: the `emit(2)` call itself throws an internal cancellation exception, so `after 2` never runs. The `finally` block still runs, which is why resources are released when you take only part of a flow.

questions.question: The screen shows nothing, even though `query` emits whenever the user types. `filters` is a cold flow that only emits when the user taps a chip. Why?
options: `combine` waits until every source has emitted once, and `filters` hasn't yet
`combine` pairs values by index, so it waits for `filters` to emit as often as `query`
`combine` needs a `StateFlow` as its first argument
`combine` collects its sources one after another, so it is stuck collecting `query`
questions.explanation: `combine` needs one value from each source before it can call the transform, so a source that hasn't emitted blocks all output. The usual fix is to give it an initial value, e.g. `filters.onStart { emit(Filters.None) }` or a `StateFlow`. Pairing by index is `zip`, not `combine`.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: `combine` emits whenever any source emits, using the latest value of each. At 200ms `b` sends `x` (latest `a` is 1), at 300ms `a` sends 2 (latest `b` is `x`), and at 400ms `b` sends `y`. `1x\n2y` would be `zip`, which pairs by index.

questions.question: In `flow.catch { emit(Error) }.collect { render(it) }`, an exception thrown inside `render` is caught by the `catch` operator.
questions.explanation: `catch` only catches exceptions from upstream (the flow and operators before it). The `collect` lambda is downstream, so its exception propagates out of `collect`. To cover it, move the work into `onEach { render(it) }` before `catch` and call `collect()` with no arguments.

questions.question: A ViewModel turns a flow of user `Action`s into a `UiState`, where each action updates the previous state. Which operator fits best, and what does it emit first?
options: `scan(initialState) { s, a -> reduce(s, a) }`, which emits `initialState` first
`fold(initialState) { ... }`, which emits each intermediate state as it is computed
`reduce { ... }`, which emits the initial state first
`map { reduce(initialState, it) }`, which keeps the previous state
questions.explanation: `scan` (the same as `runningFold`) emits the initial value and then every accumulated state, so the UI sees each step. `fold` and `reduce` are terminal operators that return only the final result, and `map` has no memory of the previous state.

questions.question: A sensor flow emits a position 100 times per second without pausing, and the UI only needs an update about every 500ms. What happens with `debounce(500)` compared to `sample(500)`?
options: `debounce` emits nothing while the stream never pauses; `sample` emits every 500ms
Both emit the latest value every 500ms
`debounce` emits the first value of each 500ms window; `sample` emits the last
`sample` waits for a 500ms pause in the stream; `debounce` emits on a fixed 500ms timer
questions.explanation: `debounce` only emits after the source has been quiet for the timeout, so a stream that never pauses emits nothing until it ends. `sample` ticks on a fixed period and emits the most recent value seen, which suits continuous streams. `debounce` is the right choice for a search box, where typing pauses.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: When `b` arrives at 100ms, `flatMapLatest` cancels the inner flow for `a`, which is still in its 300ms `delay`, so `a:done` is never emitted. `a:start` was already emitted before that, so it stays. Keeping both inner flows running is `flatMapMerge` behaviour.

questions.question: With this backoff, the API keeps failing with `IOException`. How long is the delay before the first retry, and how many times is the request made in total?
questions.explanation: `attempt` starts at 0 for the first retry, so the delays are 500, 1000 and 2000ms. Retries happen for attempts 0, 1 and 2, giving the original request plus 3 retries. On the fourth failure the predicate returns `false` and the exception goes downstream.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.explanation: `debounce(200)` emits a value only if no newer value arrives within 200ms. `k` and `ko` are replaced within 50ms, `kot` is followed by a 500ms pause so it is emitted, and `kotl` is replaced by `kotlin`. When the flow completes, `debounce` still emits the latest pending value, so `kotlin` is printed too.

questions.question: Which exceptions does the `catch` here handle?
options: Only those from `format`, the operator nearest to `collect`
questions.explanation: `catch` is transparent to downstream: it handles exceptions from everything above it in the chain, so `repo.items()` and `parse` are covered. `format` runs after `catch`, so its exceptions pass straight through to the collector. That's why `catch` usually goes near the end, just before collecting.

questions.question: In a ViewModel, `query.debounce(300).distinctUntilChanged().flatMapLatest { repo.search(it) }` drives search results. Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
options: `debounce(300)` avoids a request for every keystroke by waiting for a 300ms pause in typing
`distinctUntilChanged` skips a new search when the settled query equals the previous one, e.g. after typing a letter and deleting it
`flatMapLatest` cancels a slow in-flight search when a newer query arrives, so stale results can't overwrite newer ones
Swapping `flatMapLatest` for `flatMapMerge` gives the same results, just faster
`distinctUntilChanged` must come before `debounce` or it has no effect
questions.explanation: Each operator has its own job: `debounce` limits the request rate, `distinctUntilChanged` drops repeated settled queries, and `flatMapLatest` cancels outdated requests. `flatMapMerge` lets old requests keep running and their results can arrive out of order. Putting `distinctUntilChanged` after `debounce` is deliberate, because then it compares settled queries rather than keystrokes. The result is usually exposed with `stateIn` (day 31).

questions.question: If flow `a` emits 1, 2 and 3 quickly and only then flow `b` emits its first value `x`, `combine(a, b) { n, s -> "$n$s" }` emits `1x`, `2x` and `3x`.
questions.explanation: `combine` keeps only the latest value of each source. Until `b` has emitted, `a`'s new values just replace the stored one, so when `x` arrives the only combination emitted is `3x`. If every value of `a` must be paired, `combine` is the wrong tool.
